item.title: USA: National Science Foundation requests information on AI Research and Development Strategic Plan
item.description: On April 29, 2025, the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) requested comments on behalf of the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) among other organizations, for a 2025 National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Research and Development Strategic Plan (the Strategic Plan).The NSF outlined that the Strategic Plan would update that Strategic Plan implemented in 2023.The Strategic Plan is aimed to be aligned with the AI Action Plan introduced in February 2025. item.title: South Korea: PIPC requests strengthened personal information protection measures for large-scale processors
item.description: On April 30, 2025, the Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) requested that large-scale personal information processors implement more thorough safety measures.The PIPC highlighted that it made the request in light of the SK Telecoms customer information data breach incident. item.title: Germany: BaFin updates guidance under DORA

item.title: Malaysia: PDP publishes cross-border data transfer guidelines

item.title: Texas: Bill for genetic information security passes second reading in House
item.description: On April 29, 2025, House Bill 130 relating to genetic information security for residents was read for the second time, amended, and passed to engrossment in the Texas House of Representatives. item.title: International: UK and Japan sign Memorandum of Cooperation on quantum science and technology
item.description: On April 28, 2025, the UK Department of Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) announced that the UK and Japan signed a Memorandum of Cooperation on quantum science and technology.The Memorandum of Cooperation outlines key areas of collaboration, including:dialogue on research and innovation:interactions, academia/private sector, and funding opportunities:education, exchange, talent, and skills:security policy dialogue: recognizing quantum technologies as emerging with implications for the societal resilience and national and economic security of both countries;standards and governance: fostering regular bilateral and multilateral discussions on governance policy issues, including growing

item.title: International: Brazil and Chile sign MoU on AI
item.description: On April 22, 2025, the Brazilian Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovation (MCTI) announced that it signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on artificial intelligence (AI) with the Minister of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation of Chile.The MoU aims to establish AI systems, including a language model, that are compatible with both countries' priorities, circumstances, and particularities, with a focus on the inclusion of the various languages and cultural expressions of Latin America. item.title: USA: TAKE IT DOWN Act passes Congress
item.description: On April 28, 2025, Senate Bill 146 for the Tools to Address Known Exploitation by Immobilizing Technological Deepfakes on Websites and Networks Act (TAKE IT DOWN Act) passed the U.S. House of Representatives following its introduction to the U.S. Senate on January 16, 2025.The Act must now be signed by the President.The Act relates to the unauthorized use of digital images and non-consensual disclosure of intimate visual images.DefinitionsThe bill defines 'consent' as 'an affirmative, conscious, and voluntary authorization made by an individual free from force, fraud, duress, misrepresentation, or coercion.'A 'digital forgery' is defined as 'any intimate visual depiction of an identifiable i

item.title: Colorado: AI Consumer Protection bill introduced to Senate
item.description: On April 28, 2025, Senate Bill 318 for Artificial Intelligence (AI) Consumer Protections was introduced to the Colorado State Senate.The bill amends the Colorado AI Act which was signed by the Governor of Colorado on May 17, 2024. The Colorado AI Act enters into force on January 1, 2026.Amendments to definitionsThe bill amends the definition of algorithmic discrimination as 'the use of an artificial intelligence system that results in a violation of any applicable local, state, or federal anti-discrimination law.' item.title: International: CPPA and ICO sign declaration of cooperation on enforcement

item.title: Spain: AEPD fines Vodafone €200,000 for processing data unlawfully
item.description: On February 25, 2025, the Spanish data protection authority (AEPD) published its decision in Proceeding No. PS-00120-2024, in which it imposed a fine of €200,000 on Vodafone España, S.A.U., for violations of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), following a complaint submitted by an individual.Background to the decisionThe AEPD noted that the complainant discovered that Vodafone issued a duplicate SIM card linked to the claimant's telephone line, to unauthorized third parties. Consequently, the duplicated SIM card was used to make unauthorized transactions from the claimant's bank account. item.description: On April 24, 2025, the Dutch data protection authority (AP) requested comments on organizations' approach to artificial intelligence (AI) literacy.The AP requested feedback on practical examples of how organizations have boosted AI literacy within their organizations, including:any actions taken;what current approaches are based on, such as legislation or guidelines;whether organizations are takin

item.title: USA: FTC issues proposed order against Workado for claims regarding AI
item.description: On April 28, 2025, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) issued a proposed order against Workado, LLC for an alleged violation of Section 5(a) of the Federal Trade Commission Act (the FTC Act).Background to the proposed orderThe FTC outlined that Workado advertises, offers for sale, and sells products and services for creating marketing content, including an artificial intelligence (AI) Content Detector, and an an AI image detector. The FTC provided that Workado claimed that the AI Content Detector was developed using a wide range of material, including blog posts and Wikipedia entries, to make it more accurate for the average user. item.title: France: CNIL publishes annual report of key actions in 2024
item.description: On April 29, 2025, the French data protection authority (CNIL) published its annual report for key actions taken in 2024.CNIL highlighted that it conducted audits of public and private entities, focusing on compliance with cookies, cybersecurity, and video device regulations.CNIL provided the following summary of its regulatory actions in 2024:331 corrective measures, including:87 sanctions totaling over €55 million in fines;the simplified procedure introduced in 2022 proved effective, with 69 sanctions issued in 2024. item.title: EU: CJEU publishes summary of case law on the protection of personal data
item.description: On April 28, 2025, the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) published a Fact sheet on the protection of personal data.The Fact Sheet provides an overview of significant case law that informed data protection, both prior to and after the enactment of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).The Fact Sheet covers among other things:the right t the protection of personal data as recognized by the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU;the processing of personal data pursuant to significant case law that informed general rules for processing and key definitions;the processing of personal data within the meaning of secondary legislation such as electronic communications and crimina

item.title: Nigeria: NITDA announces approach to AI governance
item.description: On April 23, 2025, the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) announced its strategic approach to artificial intelligence (AI) governance during a panel session at the GITEX Africa 2025. NITDA emphasized the importance of integrating AI into business, organizational, and operational models to unlock new opportunities and drive smarter decision-making.NITDA highlighted its regulatory intelligence framework, which is anchored on three pillars: awareness, intelligence, and dynamism. item.title: Minnesota: Bill modifying the consumer data privacy Act introduced
item.description: On March 24, 2025, Senate Bill 2940 for an act relating to consumer protection and modifying the Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act was introduced and referred to Commerce and Consumer Protection.Scope of the LawThe bill governs the collection, processing, and sale of personal and sensitive data by legal entities conducting business in Minnesota or targeting Minnesota residents. It applies to entities that control or process personal data of 100,000 consumers or more annually or derive over 25% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data. item.title: Latvia: DVI publishes guide for social media content creators on including other people in their materials
item.description: On April 25, 2025, the Data State Inspectorate (DVI) issued guidance for social media content creators on the considerations they must consider when including other people in their materials. The DVI emphasized the importance of respecting privacy and data protection regulations when filming or photographing individuals in public or private settings.The DVI highlighted that content creators, often referred to as influencers, must ensure compliance with data protection laws if their content is intended for commercial purposes, such as promoting products or services. item.description: On April 16, 2025, the National Commission for Data Protection (CNPD) announced its decision of January 6, 2025, in which it fined a credit institution €175,000 for violation of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).Background to the decisionThe CNPD noted that it received various complaints against the company relating to the absence of responses following requests to exercise the data su

item.title: Czechia: Draft law on cybersecurity approved by Chamber of Deputies
item.description: On April 28, 2025, the National Office for Cyber and Information Security (NÚKIB) announced that on April 25, 2025, the Chamber of Deputies of the Parliament of the Czech Republic approved the draft of the new Cybersecurity Act in the third reading and is now headed to the Senate.What changes does the draft law introduce?NÚKIB explained that the draft law includes several amendments, such as transferring some powers related to the supply chain security verification mechanism from the National Agency for the Protection of Information and Communications Technology to the Government. item.title: Hamburg: HmbBfDI publishes guidance on Data Act
item.description: On April 29, 2025, the Hamburg Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information (HmbBfDI) announced the publication of a guidance titled 'The Data Act as a Challenge for Data Protection.' The guidance provides an overview of the EU Regulation on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (the Data Act), which is set to come into effect on September 12, 2025. What are the key recommendations of the guidance?The guidance, among other things, outlines example scenarios for companies under the Data Act and the options for data protection oversight. item.title: Belgium: Belgian DPA orders SPF to comply with GDPR for data transfers under FATCA
item.description: On April 24, 2025, the Belgian Data Protection Authority (Belgian DPA) issued its Decision No. 79/2025, in which the Belgian ordered the Federal Public Service for Finance (SPF) to come into compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), following a complaint from an individual.Background to the decisionThe Belgian DPA received a complaint submitted by an individual and the Accidental Americans Association of Belgium (AAAB) against SPF. item.title: Belgium: DPA reprimands Google for not dereferencing search links
item.description: On April 24, 2025, the Belgian Data Protection Authority (Belgian DPA) issued its Decision No. 77/2025, in which the Belgian DPA reprimanded Google LLC for violations of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), following a complaint from an individual.Background to the decisionThe Belgian DPA received a complaint alleging that Google refused to remove two URLs from its search results that referenced past legal issues involving the complainant. item.title: Vermont: AG files lawsuit against Clearview AI for alleged consumer protection violation
item.description: On April 25, 2025, the Vermont Attorney General (AG) announced that it refiled a lawsuit in the Vermont Superior Court, Washington Civil Division, against Clearview AI, Inc., alleging violation of the Vermont Consumer Protection Act.Background to the lawsuitThe AG alleged in the lawsuit that Clearview AI uses facial recognition technology to map the faces of Vermonters, including children, without their knowledge, and sells access to this data to its customers, in violation of the Act.
